title: 📘 UNIT 2: CLIMATE OF ETHIOPIA
notes:
Climate → the long-term average condition of the atmosphere of a place.

 Weather → the short-term condition of the atmosphere at a particular place and time.

title: 🌦️ 2.1 MEANING OF WEATHER AND CLIMATE
notes:
🌤️ Weather → the state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time. It may change within hours or days.

🌍 Climate → the average weather condition of a place observed over a long period of time.

🔄 Difference:
Weather = short-term + changes frequently.

Climate = long-term average + relatively stable pattern.

📌 Example → Today's temperature and rainfall describe weather; the usual rainfall pattern of Ethiopia describes climate.

title: 🌡️ 2.2 ELEMENTS OF WEATHER AND CLIMATE
notes:
The main elements are:

🌧️ Precipitation → water falling from the atmosphere to the Earth's surface as rain, hail, snow, etc.

🌡️ Temperature → degree of hotness or coldness of the atmosphere.

💧 Humidity → amount of water vapour present in the air.

⚖️ Air Pressure → force exerted by the weight of air on a unit area.

💨 Wind → horizontal movement of air from high-pressure areas toward low-pressure areas.

☀️ Sunshine → duration or amount of time the sun shines at a place.

☁️ Cloud Cover → portion of the sky covered by clouds.

title: 🌧️ PRECIPITATION
notes:
Precipitation → any form of water that falls from the atmosphere to the Earth's surface.

Main forms:
🌧️ Rain
❄️ Snow
🧊 Hail

📌 In Ethiopia, rainfall is the most important form of precipitation.

Factors affecting rainfall include relief, altitude, air masses, wind direction and seasonal movement of the ITCZ.

title: 🌡️ TEMPERATURE
notes:
Temperature → measure of the degree of hotness or coldness of the atmosphere.

📌 Temperature generally decreases as altitude increases.

Major controls include:
☀️ Latitude
🏔️ Altitude
🌬️ Winds
☁️ Cloud cover
🌊 Distance from large water bodies

🌡️ Temperature is commonly measured using a thermometer.

title: 💧 HUMIDITY
notes:
Humidity → amount of water vapour contained in the air.

📌 Relative humidity → amount of water vapour in the air expressed as a percentage of the maximum amount the air can hold at a given temperature.

⭐ Warm air can hold more water vapour than cold air.

💧 High humidity → air contains relatively large amounts of water vapour.

💨 Low humidity → air contains relatively small amounts of water vapour.

title: ⚖️ AIR PRESSURE
notes:
Air pressure → force exerted by the weight of the atmosphere on a unit area.

📌 Air pressure generally decreases with increasing altitude.

⬆️ High pressure → air tends to descend and spread outward.

⬇️ Low pressure → air tends to rise and surrounding air moves toward it.

⭐ Differences in air pressure help produce winds.

title: 💨 WIND
notes:
Wind → horizontal movement of air from an area of high pressure toward an area of low pressure.

📌 Wind has two important characteristics:
1️⃣ Speed → how fast the air moves.
2️⃣ Direction → the direction from which the wind blows.

💨 Wind speed → measured with an anemometer.

🧭 Wind direction → measured with a wind vane.

title: ☀️ SUNSHINE AND CLOUD COVER
notes:
☀️ Sunshine → period during which direct sunlight reaches the Earth's surface.

📌 Sunshine affects temperature, evaporation, plant growth and agricultural activities.

☁️ Cloud Cover → amount of the sky covered by clouds.

📌 Clouds affect incoming solar radiation, temperature and precipitation.

title: 🌍 2.3 CONTROLS OF WEATHER AND CLIMATE IN ETHIOPIA
notes:
The major controls include:

📍 Latitude
🏔️ Altitude
⛰️ Mountain barriers
🌍 Revolution of the Earth and inclination of Earth's axis
🌊 Distance from the sea
🌊 Ocean currents

📌 These controls influence temperature, rainfall, wind and seasonal conditions across Ethiopia.

title: 📍 LATITUDE
notes:
Latitude → angular distance north or south of the Equator.

📌 Places near the Equator generally receive more direct solar energy and have higher temperatures.

🇪🇹 Ethiopia extends across different latitudes, producing some variation in temperature and climate from north to south.

⭐ Lower latitude → generally warmer.
⭐ Higher latitude → generally cooler.

title: 🏔️ ALTITUDE
notes:
Altitude → height of a place above sea level.

📌 Temperature generally decreases as altitude increases.

🇪🇹 Ethiopia's highlands therefore have cooler conditions than nearby lowlands at lower elevations.

⭐ Altitude is one of the most important controls of Ethiopia's climate.

title: ⛰️ MOUNTAIN BARRIERS
notes:
Mountains influence climate by forcing moist air to rise.

🌧️ Windward side → rising air cools and may produce rainfall.
🏜️ Leeward side → descending air is generally drier, producing a rain-shadow effect.

🇪🇹 Ethiopia's highlands and mountain systems strongly influence the distribution of rainfall.

title: 🌍 REVOLUTION OF EARTH AND INCLINATION OF EARTH'S AXIS
notes:
🌍 Revolution → movement of the Earth around the Sun.

📐 Earth's axis is inclined at about 23.5°.

📌 The combination of Earth's revolution and axial inclination causes seasonal changes by changing the angle and duration of solar radiation received by different parts of Earth.

🇪🇹 This contributes to seasonal variation in temperature, rainfall and atmospheric conditions.

title: 🌊 DISTANCE FROM THE SEA
notes:
Distance from the sea affects temperature and moisture.

🌊 Areas close to large water bodies generally experience greater moisture influence and smaller temperature ranges.

🏜️ Areas far from the sea tend to have less maritime influence and greater continental effects.

🇪🇹 Ethiopia is landlocked, so its climate is strongly influenced by continental conditions rather than direct maritime influence.

title: 🌊 OCEAN CURRENTS
notes:
Ocean currents → large-scale movements of ocean water that transport heat.

🔥 Warm currents → generally warm and may increase moisture in nearby air.

❄️ Cold currents → generally cool surrounding air and may reduce evaporation and rainfall.

📌 Although Ethiopia has no coastline, nearby ocean and sea conditions can indirectly influence regional atmospheric circulation.

title: 🗺️ SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL VARIATION
notes:
Spatial variation → differences in weather and climate from one place to another.

⏳ Temporal variation → changes in weather and climate over time.

🇪🇹 Spatial variation in Ethiopia is strongly related to altitude, latitude, relief and moisture sources.

📅 Temporal variation occurs daily, seasonally and from year to year.

title: ⭐ DOMINANT CONTROLS OF ETHIOPIA'S CLIMATE
notes:
The most important controls of Ethiopia's climate are:

🏔️ Altitude → major influence on temperature.

📍 Latitude → influences solar energy received.

⛰️ Relief/mountain barriers → affect rainfall distribution.

🌬️ Atmospheric circulation and seasonal movement of the ITCZ → major influence on rainfall seasons.

🌍 Earth's revolution and axial inclination → contribute to seasonal changes.

⭐ KEY IDEA → Ethiopia's varied altitude and relief are major reasons for its diverse climatic conditions.

title: 🌦️ 2.4 CLIMATIC REGIONS AND SEASONAL VARIATION IN ETHIOPIA
notes:
Ethiopia has considerable climatic diversity because of differences in altitude, latitude, relief and rainfall patterns.

The section covers:
🏔️ Agro-climatic zones
☀️ Seasonal variation
🌧️ Rainfall regions.

title: 🏔️ 2.4.1 AGRO-CLIMATIC ZONES OF ETHIOPIA
notes:
Agro-climatic zones → areas classified mainly according to climate and their suitability for agricultural activities.

The traditional Ethiopian agro-climatic zones are:

❄️ Wurch (Kur)
🏔️ Dega
🌿 Woina Dega
🌾 Kolla
🏜️ Bereha

📌 Altitude is a major basis for distinguishing these zones.

title: ❄️ WURCH (KUR)
notes:
📍 Wurch/Kur → the highest and coldest agro-climatic zone.

🏔️ Very high altitude.
❄️ Very cold conditions.
🌱 Growing season is generally limited.
🐑 Livestock and cold-tolerant crops are important where conditions permit.

⭐ Remember → Wurch = highest + coldest.

title: 🏔️ DEGA
notes:
📍 Dega → highland climatic zone below Wurch.

🏔️ High altitude.
🌡️ Cool conditions.
🌧️ Generally adequate rainfall in many areas.
🌾 Suitable for crops adapted to cool highland conditions.

⭐ Remember → Dega = cool highlands.

title: 🌿 WOINA DEGA
notes:
📍 Woina Dega → intermediate highland zone.

🏔️ Medium elevation.
🌡️ Moderate temperature.
🌧️ Rainfall is generally favorable in many areas.
🌾 One of the important agricultural and settlement zones.

⭐ Remember → Woina Dega = moderate altitude + moderate climate + productive agriculture.

title: 🌾 KOLLA
notes:
📍 Kolla → lowland agro-climatic zone.

⬇️ Low altitude.
🌡️ Generally warm to hot.
🌧️ Rainfall varies considerably by region.
🌾 Agriculture and livestock activities depend strongly on available moisture.

⭐ Remember → Kolla = warm lowlands.

title: 🏜️ BEREHA
notes:
📍 Bereha → the lowest and generally hottest agro-climatic zone.

⬇️ Very low altitude.
🔥 Very hot conditions.
🌵 Generally dry or arid.
🌧️ Very low and unreliable rainfall in many areas.
🐪 Pastoralism is important in suitable areas.

⭐ Remember → Bereha = lowest + hottest + driest.

title: 📊 ALTITUDE AND TEMPERATURE IN AGRO-CLIMATIC ZONES
notes:
General relationship:

⬆️ Altitude increases → 🌡️ temperature decreases.
⬇️ Altitude decreases → 🌡️ temperature increases.

❄️ Wurch → coldest
🏔️ Dega → cool
🌿 Woina Dega → moderate
🌾 Kolla → warm/hot
🏜️ Bereha → hottest

⭐ Altitude is therefore a major basis for Ethiopia's traditional agro-climatic classification.

title: 🗺️ DISTRIBUTION AND CHARACTERISTICS OF AGRO-CLIMATIC ZONES
notes:
Agro-climatic zones are not distributed uniformly across Ethiopia.

🏔️ Highland areas → Wurch, Dega and Woina Dega are common.
⬇️ Lower elevations → Kolla is common.
🏜️ Very low and arid areas → Bereha occurs.

📌 The same zone can occur in different parts of the country because altitude and relief vary from place to place.

title: ☀️ 2.4.2 SEASONAL VARIATION
notes:
Season → a period of the year characterized by relatively distinctive weather conditions.

📌 Ethiopia's seasons are strongly associated with the seasonal movement of the sun, atmospheric circulation and rainfall patterns.

Common seasonal terms include:
🌧️ Kiremt
🌦️ Belg
☀️ Bega
🌾 Meher

title: 🌧️ KIREMT
notes:
Kiremt → the main rainy season over much of Ethiopia.

📅 Mainly June–September.
🌧️ Produces the major rainfall in much of the country.
🌾 Very important for crop production.
🌬️ Closely associated with seasonal atmospheric circulation and the northward position of the ITCZ.

⭐ Remember → Kiremt = main rainy season.

title: 🌦️ BELG
notes:
Belg → a shorter rainy season occurring mainly in parts of Ethiopia.

📅 Generally February–May, with regional variation.
🌧️ Important rainfall season in areas that receive Belg rains.
🌾 Supports agriculture and pasture.

📌 Belg rainfall is less widespread and generally less reliable than Kiremt rainfall.

title: ☀️ BEGA
notes:
Bega → dry season over much of Ethiopia.

📅 Mainly October–January.
☀️ Generally dry and sunny.
🌧️ Rainfall is low over much of the country.
🌡️ Large daily temperature ranges may occur, especially in dry areas.

⭐ Remember → Bega = mainly dry season.

title: 🌾 MEHER
notes:
Meher → the main agricultural/cropping season associated with the main rainy period in much of Ethiopia.

🌧️ Depends largely on Kiremt rainfall.
🌾 Major food crops are planted and harvested according to local rainfall and agricultural calendars.

⭐ Remember → Meher = major agricultural season.

title: ☀️ SEASONAL MOVEMENT OF THE SUN
notes:
🌍 Earth's revolution around the Sun + 23.5° axial inclination causes the apparent seasonal movement of the sun.

📌 As the overhead sun shifts north and south during the year, the distribution of solar energy changes.

🇪🇹 This seasonal movement contributes to changes in:
🌡️ Temperature
🌧️ Rainfall
💨 Atmospheric circulation
☀️ Sunshine.

title: 🌧️ SEASONAL DISTRIBUTION OF RAINFALL
notes:
Rainfall in Ethiopia is not evenly distributed throughout the year.

🌧️ Kiremt → dominant rainy season in much of the country.
🌦️ Belg → important secondary rainy season in some regions.
☀️ Bega → generally dry season.

📌 Southern and southeastern Ethiopia can have different rainfall patterns from northern and central areas because of changing atmospheric circulation and the position of the ITCZ.

title: 📉 RAINFALL VARIABILITY
notes:
Rainfall variability → differences in the amount and timing of rainfall from place to place or from one year to another.

📌 Rainfall may vary in:
📍 Amount
📅 Onset
⏳ Duration
🛑 Cessation

⚠️ High rainfall variability can cause drought, crop failure, water shortages or flooding.

🌾 Agriculture in Ethiopia is therefore strongly affected by rainfall variability.

title: 🌧️ 2.4.3 RAINFALL REGIONS
notes:
Ethiopia's rainfall varies considerably in amount, seasonality and distribution.

Major rainfall regions include:
1️⃣ Summer Rainfall Region
2️⃣ Double Maximum Rainfall Region
3️⃣ Tropical Rainfall Region
4️⃣ Winter Rainfall Region

📌 These regions are mainly distinguished by the timing and distribution of rainfall.

title: 🌧️ SUMMER RAINFALL REGION
notes:
📍 Covers much of the central, northern and western highlands and adjoining areas.

🌧️ Most rainfall occurs during the summer months.
📅 Main rainy period → Kiremt.
🌾 Important for Meher agriculture.

⭐ Key idea → one dominant summer rainfall maximum.

title: 🌦️ DOUBLE MAXIMUM RAINFALL REGION
notes:
📍 Mainly found in areas where rainfall has two distinct peaks during the year.

🌧️ Two rainfall maxima occur because of seasonal movement of atmospheric rain-producing systems.
🌾 The two rainy periods can support more than one agricultural season in suitable areas.

⭐ Key idea → two rainfall peaks in one year.

title: 🌴 TROPICAL RAINFALL REGION
notes:
📍 Mainly associated with southern and southwestern parts of Ethiopia.

🌧️ Rainfall can occur during much of the year, with seasonal variations.
🌡️ Warm tropical conditions dominate.
🌱 Natural vegetation can be relatively dense where moisture is sufficient.

⭐ Key idea → tropical conditions + longer/more distributed rainfall.

title: ☔ WINTER RAINFALL REGION
notes:
📍 A limited area of Ethiopia receives a significant proportion of rainfall during the winter period.

🌧️ Rainfall occurs mainly during the cooler months compared with the main summer-rainfall areas.

📌 Winter rainfall patterns are influenced by regional atmospheric circulation and moisture-bearing systems.

⭐ Key idea → rainfall maximum occurs during winter rather than summer.

title: 📊 RAINFALL VARIABILITY IN ETHIOPIA
notes:
Rainfall varies spatially and temporally.

📍 Spatial variability → wetter highland and southwestern areas generally contrast with drier northeastern and southeastern lowlands.

📅 Temporal variability → rainfall changes between seasons and from year to year.

⚠️ Consequences of abnormal rainfall:
🌾 Crop failure
🐄 Livestock losses
💧 Water shortages
🌊 Flooding
🏜️ Drought.

title: 🌍 INTER-TROPICAL CONVERGENCE ZONE (ITCZ)
notes:
ITCZ → a zone near the Equator where major tropical air masses converge.

💨 Air converges and rises in the ITCZ.
☁️ Rising moist air produces clouds and rainfall.

📌 The ITCZ shifts northward and southward with the apparent movement of the sun.

🇪🇹 Its seasonal movement strongly influences the timing and distribution of rainfall in Ethiopia.

⭐ Northward movement → brings rain-producing conditions to northern parts.
⭐ Southward movement → shifts the rainfall belt southward.

title: 🌡️ 2.5 MEASUREMENTS OF WEATHER AND CLIMATE
notes:
Weather elements are measured using specific instruments:

🌡️ Temperature → Thermometer
🌧️ Rainfall → Rain gauge
⚖️ Air pressure → Barometer
💨 Wind speed → Anemometer
🧭 Wind direction → Wind vane

📌 Measurements are recorded systematically to study weather conditions and long-term climate patterns.

title: 🌡️ MEASURING AND RECORDING TEMPERATURE
notes:
🌡️ Temperature is measured using a thermometer.

📌 Temperature may be recorded at specific times or continuously using suitable instruments.

Common temperature measures:
🌡️ Maximum temperature → highest temperature recorded during a period.
🌡️ Minimum temperature → lowest temperature recorded during a period.

⭐ Temperature data help determine climatic conditions and agricultural suitability.

title: 🌡️ THERMOMETER
notes:
Thermometer → instrument used to measure air temperature.

📌 Temperature is commonly expressed in degrees Celsius (°C).

Uses:
🌡️ Measuring air temperature.
📊 Recording maximum and minimum temperatures.
🌍 Comparing temperatures between places and seasons.

title: 🌧️ MEASURING AND RECORDING RAINFALL
notes:
Rainfall is measured as the depth of water received over a given area during a specific period.

📌 Unit → millimetres (mm).

Rainfall measurements help determine:
🌾 Agricultural conditions
💧 Water availability
🌊 Flood risk
🏜️ Drought conditions

⭐ Rainfall is measured using a rain gauge.

title: 🌧️ RAIN GAUGE
notes:
Rain gauge → instrument used to collect and measure rainfall.

📌 Rainfall is usually recorded in millimetres (mm).

Basic principle → rain is collected in a container and the depth of collected water is measured.

⭐ More rainfall → greater measured depth.
⭐ Less rainfall → smaller measured depth.

title: 🧮 TOTAL ANNUAL RAINFALL
notes:
Total annual rainfall → sum of the rainfall received during all months of a year.

Formula:
Total Annual Rainfall = January rainfall + February rainfall + ... + December rainfall.

📌 If monthly rainfall values are given, add all 12 monthly values to obtain the annual total.

title: 🧮 MEAN ANNUAL RAINFALL
notes:
Mean annual rainfall → average annual rainfall calculated over a number of years.

Formula:
Mean Annual Rainfall = Sum of annual rainfall values ÷ Number of years.

📌 It gives a better indication of the long-term average rainfall of a place than a single year's rainfall.

title: ⚖️ MEASURING AND RECORDING AIR PRESSURE
notes:
Air pressure is measured using a barometer.

📌 Air pressure is commonly expressed in millibars (mb) or hectopascals (hPa).

⭐ Pressure generally decreases with altitude.
⭐ Differences in air pressure contribute to wind movement.

title: ⚖️ BAROMETER
notes:
Barometer → instrument used to measure atmospheric/air pressure.

📌 Uses:
⚖️ Measuring air pressure.
🌦️ Monitoring changes in atmospheric conditions.
🌧️ Helping in weather forecasting.

⭐ High and low pressure systems are important in understanding weather.

title: 💨 MEASURING AND RECORDING WIND SPEED
notes:
Wind speed → rate at which air moves over a given distance.

📌 Wind speed is measured using an anemometer.

Common units include:
➡️ metres per second (m/s)
➡️ kilometres per hour (km/h)

⭐ Strong pressure differences generally produce stronger winds.

title: 💨 ANEMOMETER
notes:
Anemometer → instrument used to measure wind speed.

📌 A common cup anemometer has rotating cups that turn according to wind speed.

⭐ Faster rotation → stronger wind.
⭐ Slower rotation → weaker wind.

title: 🧭 MEASURING WIND DIRECTION
notes:
Wind direction → direction from which the wind originates.

📌 It is important to distinguish wind direction from the direction toward which air moves.

Example:
🌬️ A north wind → wind coming FROM the north.

⭐ Wind direction is measured using a wind vane.

title: 🧭 WIND VANE
notes:
Wind vane → instrument used to determine wind direction.

📌 The vane aligns with the wind and points toward the direction from which the wind is coming.

Common directions:
N → North
NE → Northeast
E → East
SE → Southeast
S → South
SW → Southwest
W → West
NW → Northwest.

title: 🎯 UNIT 2 QUICK REVISION
notes:
🌦️ Weather → short-term atmospheric condition.
🌍 Climate → long-term average weather.

🌧️ Precipitation → water falling from atmosphere.
🌡️ Temperature → degree of hotness/coldness.
💧 Humidity → water vapour in air.
⚖️ Air pressure → force exerted by air.
💨 Wind → horizontal movement of air.
☀️ Sunshine → duration of sunlight.
☁️ Cloud cover → portion of sky covered by clouds.

🏔️ Main climate controls → latitude, altitude, mountain barriers, Earth's revolution and axial inclination, distance from sea, ocean currents.

🏔️ Agro-climatic zones → Wurch, Dega, Woina Dega, Kolla, Bereha.

☀️ Seasons → Kiremt, Belg, Bega; Meher refers mainly to the major agricultural season.

🌧️ Rainfall regions → Summer, Double Maximum, Tropical and Winter rainfall regions.

🌍 ITCZ → shifting convergence zone that strongly influences Ethiopian rainfall.

🌡️ Instruments → Thermometer = temperature; Rain gauge = rainfall; Barometer = air pressure; Anemometer = wind speed; Wind vane = wind direction.
